pull.title: feat(desktop): mcc-desktop --print-status, the JSON status surface (6.42.0)
pull.body:
**Spec:** `specs/PR-DESKTOP-WEBVIEW-SPEC.md` §2.1, §6.1 (C1–C3, C9, C10), §6.2, §6.5 row **S1**. Version **6.42.0** (MINOR — new user-facing CLI surface).

## What and why

A desktop shell (S2) renders `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/admin` in a second process. That process must never decide where the config lives, which port to use, or how long to wait for a restart. `resolve_config_dir()` (`config/paths.py:295`) is a *policy*, not a lookup — `MCC_CONFIG_DIR`, then `~/.mcc`, then `~/.fcc` only if it passes four checks, two of which open the SQLite request log and construct a whole `Settings`. Reimplementing any of that in Rust is the single most likely way this design decays.

So the shell asks Python. `mcc-desktop --print-status` (and the `fcc-desktop` alias) prints **one JSON document** on stdout and exits `0`.

```console
$ mcc-desktop --print-status
{
  "schema": 1,
  "version": "6.42.0",
  "config_dir": "C:\\Users\\me\\.mcc",
  "config_dir_source": "current",
  "config_dir_is_legacy": false,
  "host": "127.0.0.1",
  "port": 8082,
  "root_url": "http://127.0.0.1:8082",
  "admin_url": "http://127.0.0.1:8082/admin",
  "health_url": "http://127.0.0.1:8082/health",
  "server_presence": "healthy",
  "port_conflict": null,
  "server_mode": "spawn",
  "window": "auto",
  "window_open": true,
  "window_width": 1400,
  "window_height": 900,
  "tray_enabled": true,
  "minimize_to_tray": false,
  "start_at_login": false,
  "server_log": "C:\\Users\\me\\.mcc\\logs\\server.log",
  "start_timeout_seconds": 15.0,
  "health_check_interval_seconds": 0.25,
  "health_poll_seconds": 5.0,
  "health_failure_threshold": 3,
  "activation_poll_seconds": 1.0,
  "reconnect_timeout_seconds": 1040.0
}
```

**No new logic.** `cli/desktop_status.py` only spells existing answers as JSON.

## Schema table — key → type → source

| key | type | source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `schema` | int | `cli/desktop_status.py:46` (`STATUS_SCHEMA`) |
| `version` | string | `core/version.py:21` `package_version()` |
| `config_dir` | string | `config/paths.py:423` → `:295` `resolve_config_dir()` |
| `config_dir_source` | string — `env`/`current`/`legacy`/`created` | `config/paths.py:122` |
| `config_dir_is_legacy` | bool | `config/paths.py:129` `uses_legacy_home` |
| `host` | string | `config/server_urls.py:6` `local_browser_host()` (bind at `config/settings.py:1205`) |
| `port` | int | `config/settings.py:1206` |
| `root_url` | string | `config/server_urls.py:23` |
| `admin_url` | string | `config/server_urls.py:29` |
| `health_url` | string | `root_url` + `api/routes.py:268` `/health` |
| `server_presence` | string — `healthy`/`free`/`foreign` | `cli/desktop.py:92` `probe_server_presence()` |
| `port_conflict` | string \| null | `cli/desktop.py:110` `port_conflict_message()` |
| `server_mode` | string — `spawn`/`attach`/`off` | `config/desktop.py:53` via `:68` |
| `window` | string — `auto`/`app-mode`/`pywebview`/`browser` | `config/desktop.py:54` |
| `window_open` | bool | `config/desktop.py:55` |
| `window_width` | int | `config/settings.py:1278` |
| `window_height` | int | `config/settings.py:1281` |
| `tray_enabled` | bool | `config/desktop.py:50` |
| `minimize_to_tray` | bool | `config/desktop.py:52` |
| `start_at_login` | bool | `config/desktop.py:51` |
| `server_log` | string | `config/paths.py:515` `server_log_path()` |
| `start_timeout_seconds` | float | `config/settings.py:1251` |
| `health_check_interval_seconds` | float | `config/settings.py:1245` |
| `health_poll_seconds` | float | `config/settings.py:1267` |
| `health_failure_threshold` | int | `config/settings.py:1273` |
| `activation_poll_seconds` | float | `config/settings.py:1261` |
| `reconnect_timeout_seconds` | float | `config/constants.py:333` + `config/settings.py:1224` |

Three keys are additions to the spec's §2.1 sketch, each because a shell provably needs it: `config_dir_is_legacy` (the spec's "legacy flag"), `minimize_to_tray` and `health_poll_seconds` (C9's debounce is *threshold × poll interval*, and the threshold alone does not give a duration), plus `window_width`/`window_height` for §2.4's first-run geometry. `version` is emitted; **`latest` is deliberately omitted** — it needs a GitHub call or an in-process cache that a fresh `--print-status` subprocess cannot see, and the spec's own rule is that this command makes no network call off the machine. The shell reads `latest` from `/admin/api/version` once it is attached, like the dashboard does.

## Contract mapping

| # | Contract | Enforced by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **C1** | The shell never resolves the config dir, port or admin URL itself | `tests/contracts/test_config_dir_is_single_sourced.py::test_shell_source_never_names_the_config_dir` — greps `desktop-shell/**` for `.mcc`, `.fcc`, `MCC_CONFIG_DIR`, `8082`. Skips (green) until S2 creates that tree, so S2 inherits the guard instead of having to remember it. |
| **C2** | `--print-status` is read-only | `test_does_not_acquire_the_singleton_lock` (`InterprocessFileLock.__init__` raises), `test_does_not_write_desktop_json` (every writer + `subprocess.Popen` raises; the config dir listing is byte-identical before and after), `test_does_not_touch_the_windows_registry` (every writing `winreg` call recorded; recorder must stay empty) |
| **C3** | Every documented key present; `schema` bumped on removal/retype | `test_emits_every_documented_key` — `tuple(payload) == STATUS_KEYS` **and** a per-key type map, so a retype fails exactly like a removal |
| **C9** | Debounce and reconnect budget come from `--print-status`, never hard-coded | keys `health_failure_threshold`, `health_poll_seconds`, `reconnect_timeout_seconds`; `test_reconnect_budget_follows_the_configured_drain` pins the number to `release_updates`' own formula (`cli` may not import `application`, so it is recomputed from `config/constants.py:333`, not copied) |
| **C10** | `--status` output unchanged byte-for-byte | untouched code path; `tests/cli/test_desktop_mode.py` unchanged and green |

## Tests

`tests/cli/test_desktop_print_status.py` — 12 tests, the eight the spec names plus four:

- `test_emits_every_documented_key` (golden key set + type map)
- `test_reports_healthy_foreign_and_free` (drives the real ladder from `preflight_proxy`/`probe_port_available`, not a stub of the ladder)
- `test_carries_the_port_conflict_message_when_foreign`
- `test_does_not_acquire_the_singleton_lock`
- `test_does_not_write_desktop_json`
- `test_honours_MCC_CONFIG_DIR`
- `test_reports_a_legacy_fcc_home`
- `test_maps_a_wildcard_bind_to_loopback`
- `test_prints_one_json_document_and_exits_zero` *(added — stdout is a machine's input)*
- `test_never_prints_a_key_or_a_token` *(added — safe to paste into a bug report)*
- `test_does_not_touch_the_windows_registry` *(added — a full-suite run recently deleted a developer's real HKCU `Run` value; this command above all must be safe on a live machine)*
- `test_reconnect_budget_follows_the_configured_drain` *(added — C9)*

`tests/contracts/test_startup_import_cost.py::test_print_status_imports_nothing_heavyweight` *(added)* — a fresh subprocess that answers `--print-status` must not have loaded `openai`, `openpyxl`, `aiohttp`, `tiktoken`, `api.admin_routes`, `api.app`, `application.release_updates` or `pystray`. A shell calls this on every launch and every reconnect; its cost is paid over and over.

## Docs

`README.md` (Desktop App — a "Scripting it" subsection), `docs/USAGE.md` (the CLI list plus a full `#machine-readable-status` field walkthrough with the `schema` rule), `ARCHITECTURE.md` (the desktop layer now names `cli/desktop_status.py`), and the in-dashboard Guide's **Desktop & RTK** section.

## Not verified here

- No shell exists yet, so C1's grep has nothing to scan and C9 is enforced only on the producing side. Both become live in S2.
- `latest` is absent by design (above), not by oversight.
- The local full-suite run was done with `APPDATA`/`LOCALAPPDATA` redirected to a scratch tree and with the three `winreg`-reaching test files skipped, because the suite is not yet hermetic against the real registry; Linux CI covers them.

commit.message:
feat(desktop): mcc-desktop --print-status, the JSON status surface (6.42.0)

A desktop shell renders the dashboard in a second process, and that process must
never work out where the config lives, which port to use, or how long to wait for
a restart. `resolve_config_dir()` is not a lookup, it is a policy -- MCC_CONFIG_DIR,
then ~/.mcc, then ~/.fcc only if it passes four checks, two of which open a SQLite
request log and build a whole Settings. Reimplementing any part of that outside
Python is how this design decays.

So it asks Python. `mcc-desktop --print-status` (and `fcc-desktop --print-status`)
prints one JSON document on stdout and exits 0: schema, version, the config
directory with how it was chosen and whether it is the legacy home, the
loopback-mapped host, port, root/admin/health URLs, the healthy|free|foreign
presence of the port (with the port-conflict message naming the holding process
when it is foreign), every desktop preference, the server log path, and the five
timing numbers -- including the health debounce threshold and the 1040 s reconnect
budget a window must read rather than compile in, or a routine self-update repaints
as a dead server.

Nothing here is new logic. cli/desktop_status.py only spells existing answers as
JSON: config/paths.py stays the single source of the directory, config/server_urls.py
of the browser-facing URL (its host mapper is now public -- 0.0.0.0 is a bind, not
an address a window can navigate to), cli/desktop.py:92 of the presence ladder,
config/desktop.py of the preferences, config/constants.py of the reconnect budget.
`cli` may not import `application`, so the budget is recomputed from the same parts
and a test pins it to what release_updates reports to the dashboard.

It is a pure read (C2): no spawn, no singleton lock, no write to desktop.json, no
autostart reconciliation, no registry call, no server start -- proven by tests that
make each of those explode. It carries no key, token or secret, so it is safe to
paste into a bug report. It is also cheap: a subprocess contract asserts that
answering --print-status loads neither openai, openpyxl, aiohttp, tiktoken, the
admin routes, the ASGI app, release_updates nor pystray, because a shell calls it
on every launch and every reconnect.

`schema` is the compatibility handle: bumped when a documented key is removed or
retyped, not when one is added. STATUS_KEYS is the golden set and a test compares
it against a real payload key-for-key and type-for-type (C3), so neither can drift
silently. `--status`'s five key=value lines are untouched (C10).

C1's grep contract for the future shell tree lands here too, skipping while
desktop-shell/ does not exist -- so the PR that writes the shell inherits a green
guard against a hard-coded 8082 or ~/.mcc rather than having to remember to add one.

Spec: specs/PR-DESKTOP-WEBVIEW-SPEC.md S1 (contracts C1-C3, C9, C10).
